hypothesis: Stable previous-byte grouping improves complete Deflate frame costs on raw opening250KB when queue lengths are reconstructed from a histogram and one stored final byte.
mechanism: Begin with predecessor0. Append every raw byte to its predecessor's FIFO bucket, then concatenate buckets in byte order. Transmit the final raw byte. Bucket v has size histogram(v)+[v=0]-[v=last]. The decoder follows the same predecessor path through the queues, checks full consumption and exact final byte. Definitions, dictionaries and a256-count table are unnecessary.
scope: A whole-raw-byte bounded-frame ordering experiment, distinct from retired direct WRT token BWT side channels, numeric extraction, grammar selection, enumeration and interpreter-context replacement. No claim of inventing context sorting or of an achieved corpus ratio.
controls: K: compute the bucket transform and exact inverse, then emit exactly P
D: use the transformed payload only when the complete new frame is strictly smaller; otherwise exact P fallback
budgets: One fixed mechanism and opening250KB development population. Synthetic inverse, malformed queue and full-driver tests first. Freeze measured source/runtime identities and CPU2 memory/scratch/elapsed limits before the published canonical corpus job.
next_decision: Measure transformed candidate costs even when rejected, exact inverse and raw repeats, and command-specific source inventory. A strict archive gain permits separately frozen fresh250KB confirmation; equality or loss triggers a different evidence-based exploration rather than ending the search. No larger launch without its own frozen decision and resource admission.
preservation: Keep sealed source and receipts unchanged, preserve HORIZON and other owners, install nothing. Use project-owned temporary directories because /tmp write probes return EDQUOT.
